name: proxy

proxy.description: The harness proxy: {op: request, wire?, body} forwards a model request through the harness and tools; {op: launch, agent, model, args, passthrough?} renders an agent launch aimed at this proxy's HTTP listener, or with passthrough one whose base URLs relay through this proxy, enriched, to the upstreams in bases without the router; context, trace and usage report on one exchange by id.

description: Serves authenticated loopback model API requests through the router, harness, tools, and memory.

record_usage.doc: Persist an automatic usage journal for every request.

usage_accounting.doc: Add cumulative model-usage reports to native responses.

tool_trace.doc: Record a trace of every tool call a request made.

yolo.doc: Automatic execution: grant every tool call without asking the policy. The same meaning the agent's `yolo` has, for a launched agent whose own client already governs its calls.

ledger.doc: Memory key each completed exchange is appended to as `{op: "ledger", action: "append"}` (normally `memory`); empty sends nothing and needs nothing. A key named here must be an event some cartridge in the composition listens to.

context_recall.doc: Offer recalled context to the model alongside the request.

context_limits.deadline_ms.doc: How long context assembly may take before it answers with what it has.

context_limits.max_rows.doc: Evidence rows one assembly may carry.

context_limits.max_bytes.doc: Bytes those rows may take together.

client_key_envs.doc: Named HTTP principals mapped to the environment variable holding each secret. Secrets are read at listener startup, never from this file.

tools.doc: Exact tool keys this proxy grants. Empty means every `tool.*` event the composition listens to.

cwd.doc: Working directory a launched agent runs in.

key_env.doc: Environment variable holding the key that authenticates the listener.

listen.doc: Loopback address the proxy serves, or nothing. The host binds it (the manifest names it as `listener`) and hands the node the socket, so the address and its queued connections survive a reload of this cartridge and a `daemon --replace`. Port 0 takes a port once and keeps it for this project.

max_steps.doc: Model round trips one request may take.

max_tool_calls.doc: Tool calls one request may make.

timeout_secs.doc: How long one request may run. `events.proxy.timeout_ms` is this default plus a 60s grace (1860000), so an event-bus caller receives the proxy's own diagnosed deadline instead of the host's bare timeout; that event bound covers every `proxy` op, while only `request` carries this inner deadline. Raising `timeout_secs` past 1860 puts the host's `event_timeout_ms` back in front.

max_bytes.doc: Largest request body accepted. A caller-owned history on a long-context route is legitimately large; this is the resource guard, not the context ceiling.
